requirements.text: Runs scenario 05's crawl under a name/ID the program chooses, with the crawl's state kept between processes.
Started again with the same name after a kill, the crawl continues where it stopped (neither starting afresh nor silently doing nothing).
The dataset ends with every book exactly once: no duplicate from requests re-run after the kill or from the retry.
Retries only the requests that failed in that crawl (not the successes), once: later starts do not retry again on their own.
A run with nothing left to do says that nothing was done and why, instead of finishing silently.
While the crawl runs, prints what is in flight and what is waiting, and why it waits.

api_misuses.assumed: yields each request's superseding outcome so a retried request that succeeded is removed from the 'still failed' list (the else branch)
api_misuses.doc_says: the filter reads only outcomes of the listed kinds, so a later success is never seen and the else branch is dead: retried successes are still printed as 'still failed' (output only)

programs.notes: Same ID resumes; retryFailed once, guarded by startedAs and a Key-value store flag; an ended start prints nothingDone's reason; progress lists inFlight and waiting with reason and setting. Relies on import.meta.main to run main (Node 24.2+), and the 'still failed' listing is misleading.

Mirrors the golden: resume by ID, retry_failed only when not started as ended, nothing_done reason printed, progress with in_flight and waiting reasons; prints the nothing-done line twice in some paths.

api_misuses.assumed: safe to call on every start, including one whose Run started_as Ended
api_misuses.doc_says: it re-admits every failed request and returns an ended Run to running (and started_as says a call giving an Ended Run new work throws RunEndedError), so a third start with leftover failures retries again or fails instead of reporting nothing done

programs.notes: Resume, serve with progress and dataset check are right, but retry_failed is called unconditionally on every start, so the failures are retried on each later run rather than once; the nothing-done message only appears when no failure is left.

Replaces JOBDIR with its own flushed journal and a URL-deduplicating dataset pipeline, which survive even a SIGKILL; retry is a separate 'retry NAME' command that re-issues only failed URLs, and a finished crawl prints 'nothing was done' with the reason; an extension prints in-flight and queued requests with the slot concurrency/delay reason.

Named RequestQueue/KeyValueStore survive purgeOnStart; failures are re-added once under '#retry' keys with a retries marker; the dataset is deduplicated by URL after each crawl; an empty queue with no unretried failure prints 'Nothing was done' and why; status shows in-flight requests and the autoscaled pool's reason.

Resume by ID, retryFailed only when failed > 0 and not started as ended, nothing-done reason printed (with a fallback for an ended start), progress with inFlight and waiting reasons. The single progress loop ends with the first finish, so the retry phase is not printed; relies on import.meta.main.

Same shape as the golden: resume by ID, one retry_failed guarded by started_as, progress with in_flight and waiting reasons and settings, nothing_done explained; also handles SIGTERM by cancelling into async with.

Resume by ID with serve and throttled progress; the retry is a separate 'retry' invocation, relying on retry_failed's documented return of an ended Run to running (startedAs's RunEndedError rule makes this slightly ambiguous); an ended start without the argument prints nothing_done's reason.

JOBDIR plus an in_flight.json re-sent on resume and a URL-deduplicating pipeline; '--retry-failed' re-sends only the failure ledger with dont_filter; a finished job prints 'Nothing done' and why; status prints transferring requests and the delay/concurrency reason for queued ones. Like the golden, a SIGKILL can still lose JOBDIR queue state.

Resume via a named queue and per-URL push deduplication work, and an idle run says nothing was done; but every start moves all stored failures into a new retry round, so requests that failed again are retried on each later run instead of once, and a Ctrl+C in the crawl phase (Crawlee's pause resolves run()) goes straight into the retry phase.
